column2: On the authority of Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood of a Muslim person is not lawful except in one of three cases: the married adulterer, a life for a life, and the one who leaves his religion and separates from the community.”
“The blood of a person is not lawful”: it is not permissible to shed his blood.
What is meant is the prohibition of killing him, even without shedding his blood.
Muslim: in one narration, “who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah”; this is an explanatory description.
“Except in one of three”: qualities for which the ruler must carry out the death penalty, because of the general welfare in it, namely the preservation of lives, lineages and religion.
“The married adulterer”: one who has married and had intercourse within a valid marriage and then commits adultery after that; he is stoned until he dies.
“A life for a life”: one who kills deliberately without right is killed, on condition of equivalence in religion and freedom;
so a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever, nor a free man for a slave.
“The one who leaves his religion”: [leaves] Islam by apostasy.
“And separates from the community”: the community of the Muslims.

The blood of a Muslim becomes lawful only through one of three kinds [of act]: leaving the religion of Islam; killing a soul, under the conditions mentioned above; and violating the sanctity of what is unlawful through adultery after intercourse within a valid marriage.
It is permissible to describe a person by what he formerly was and has since left, since the apostate is excepted from the Muslims, in consideration of what he was before leaving his religion.
